proof_coverage.claim: Main cancellation statement, quantified setting, and reduction
proof_coverage.status: Checked within the paper's cited representability and existing cancellation inputs
hypotheses: Smooth affine scheme X over an algebraically closed field k.
Dimension d >= 3 and d! invertible in k; in positive characteristic this means char(k)>d.
Two vector bundles both of rank d-1, with an arbitrary common stable class; no trivial-determinant or stably-free hypothesis is inserted.
reasoning: The claimed injectivity concerns stabilization s_{d-1} from rank d-1 bundles to rank d bundles. Previously established cancellation at rank d and above turns one-step cancellation into the assertion for any stable isomorphism.

Representability identifies rank n bundles with A1-homotopy classes into BGL_n, and stable reduced K-theory with BGL. The proof must therefore handle fibers over every stable bundle, rather than only the trivial fiber.
The key new vanishing is H^d(X, pi_d^A1(A^d minus 0)(L))=0. Untwisting reduces this to the un-twisted group, and the proof combines divisibility and annihilation by the same integer d!(d-1)!.
This combination is logically sufficient: if N G=0 and G=N G, each g=N h=0. Divisibility alone would not suffice.
The determinant of the selected bundle is retained as a coefficient twist throughout the two Postnikov stages.
boundaries: The proof initially treats a connected smooth scheme. For a disjoint union, bundle classification and the relevant cohomology split by components. Components of top dimension use the stated result; on lower-dimensional components the rank d-1 is at least the component dimension, where the earlier cancellation input applies. No connectedness counterexample was found.
Neither singular affine schemes, nonalgebraically closed base fields, nor primes dividing d! are inferred to satisfy the main theorem from this review.

proof_coverage.claim: Exact actions in a fibration and change of mapping-space basepoint
reasoning: For F -> E -> B, a fiber of homotopy classes is an orbit set under the loop action, and the stabilizer description at a general lift requires using that lift as the basepoint.
Section 2.1 explicitly changes the basepoint and translates in the abelian group object E. The resulting map q_*^gamma is retained rather than silently replaced by the original based map.
This distinction matters in the application: cancellation of an arbitrary bundle cannot be obtained merely by computing the fiber of the trivial stable class.
The later Chern-class formula for the shifted obstruction supplies the nontrivial-bundle dependence needed by this basepoint change.

proof_coverage.claim: Twisted Eilenberg-MacLane spaces and the relative mapping-space fiber
proof_coverage.status: Checked with the relative interpretation explicit on page 10
reasoning: K^G(A,n)=EG x_G K(A,n) is used over BG, with a specified G-torsor P on X. The homotopy fiber over its fixed classifying map gives cohomology with local coefficients A(P).
Lemma 2.2.2 concerns the mapping-space fiber with that torsor fixed. Page 10 explicitly phrases the calculation in terms of derived mapping spaces over X_+.

An unbased fiber of a map of sets without a fixed torsor identification could have an additional automorphism quotient. That alternative interpretation is not used to manufacture a defect, because the relative setting needed by the proof is specified.

The Moore-Postnikov tower uses the fiber homotopy sheaves with their fundamental-group action, and its k-invariants classify the twisted principal stages. The simply connected fiber hypothesis and indexing were tracked into the BGL application.
external_inputs: Existence and convergence of the motivic Moore-Postnikov tower and the cited A1 representability formalism are accepted as stated inputs rather than reconstructed foundations.

proof_coverage.claim: Linear-group fiber sequence and canonical top-degree untwisting
reasoning: The fiber of BGL_n -> BGL_{n+1} is A^{n+1} minus 0, with the G_m action obtained by rescaling the first coordinate. The induced coefficient action is retained.

For Lemma 2.2.3, the final Rost-Schmid term is a sum over closed points. Every closed-point residue field is k, and a change of generator in a line fiber is a square over algebraically closed k. The action of a square is trivial, giving a canonical identification of the last chain terms.

A canonical identification of the last terms alone is not enough; the images of the incoming differentials must coincide. For each codimension-(d-1) integral curve, take its finite normalization C. It is a smooth affine curve over the perfect algebraically closed field.

Pic(C) is 2-divisible, so the pulled-back line bundle has a square root. The corresponding curve Rost-Schmid diagram identifies its contribution to the two boundary images. Summing these contributions proves the required top-cohomology identification.
This does not require a canonical global identification of every term of the two complexes. The proof needs and supplies equality of the incoming images in the canonical final term.
external_inputs: The square-action rule, the Rost-Schmid resolution, and the transfers used in the normalization diagram are standard cited inputs and were not reconstructed from their foundational definitions.

proof_coverage.claim: Stable cohomotopy range and coordinate power-map degree
proof_coverage.status: Checked with dimension bounds kept explicit
reasoning: A^d minus 0 is (d-2)-connected and its first nonzero sheaf is pi_{d-1}=K_d^MW. Its A1 self-map group is GW(k), with the identity corresponding to 1.
If sqrt(-1) belongs to k, the degree n_epsilon of the coordinate power map equals n in GW(k). The induced operation on the appropriate suspended groups is multiplication by n.
Lemma 2.3.3 only asserts this for 2 <= m <= 2d-4. In particular m=d is allowed only for d>=4. The later proof respects this and treats d=3 separately.
For a target that is (n-1)-connected, Proposition 2.3.1 requires source A1-cohomological dimension at most 2n-2. Substituting n=d-1 gives the bound 2d-4.

A coordinate power map need not be literally G_m-equivariant as a map of spaces under the same action on both sides. Its induced homotopy-sheaf map in the stated range is n times the identity, which is equivariant; this is sufficient for the twisted coefficient operation used later.

proof_coverage.claim: The split quadric, Suslin maps, and the factorial cokernel bound
proof_coverage.status: Checked modulo the explicitly cited Suslin construction
reasoning: The projection Q_{2n-1}={sum x_i y_i=1} -> A^n minus 0 is Zariski locally an A^{n-1}-bundle: on x_i nonzero, solve for y_i and use the other y coordinates freely. Thus the asserted A1 equivalence is justified by an affine-bundle structure, not merely by identifying set-theoretic fibers.
Suslin's u'_d:Q_{2d-1}->GL_d stabilizes to u_d, and the first-row composite r_d u'_d is the coordinate power map of exponent (d-1)! up to the specified equivalence.
Consequently, in the stable homotopy range, the image of the induced cohomology map contains (d-1)! times every class. Lemma 2.4.1's cokernel is therefore annihilated by (d-1)!.
Applications later use the sphere dimensions d, d+1, or d+2 separately. The factorial and the allowed homotopy degree must both be shifted with the sphere dimension.
external_inputs: The explicit Suslin matrices and their cited homotopies are not rederived entry by entry. The proof audit checks the consequences of the relations as stated.

proof_coverage.claim: Connectivity and low homotopy sheaves of the stabilization fibers F_i
proof_coverage.status: Checked against the paper's exact sequences and parity conventions
reasoning: F_i is the fiber of BGL_i->BGL, and the fiber sequence A^d minus 0 -> F_{d-1} -> F_d controls the unstable stabilization step.

The first nonzero sheaf of F_{d-1} is in degree d-1. Its expression is K_d^MW for odd d and K_d^M for even d; the additional kernel appearing in the even case is handled by a power of the fundamental ideal.

For the smooth d-dimensional scheme over algebraically closed k with char(k) different from 2, I^m restricted to X vanishes for m>=d+1. Hence the relevant twists of the first sheaf reduce to K_d^M on X.
The reduction does not erase the determinant before it is legitimate: the G_m action and the ideal-sheaf vanishing are first accounted for.
Theorem 3.0.3 is the key new top-cohomology vanishing, deferred to Section 4; it is not used as if already independently proved.
external_inputs: The known homotopy-sheaf calculations of F_i, the Milnor-Witt/fundamental-ideal exact sequences, and the cohomological-dimension bound for the relevant fields are accepted cited inputs.

proof_coverage.claim: Top-cohomology comparison and truncation to the last two obstruction stages
reasoning: Once H^d(X,pi_d(A^d minus 0)(L)) vanishes, Corollary 3.0.4 identifies the two top cohomology groups for pi_d(F_{d-1})(L) and pi_d(F_d)(L).

The use of top cohomology here factors through the image sheaf; cohomological dimension at most d makes H^d right exact on a short exact sequence. It does not require a false general assertion that H^d preserves arbitrary three-term kernels.
Only stages d-1 and d of the Moore-Postnikov tower contribute to bundle classification on a d-dimensional affine scheme. Higher obstruction groups lie above the cohomological dimension.
The comparison with the original BGL_{d-1} mapping set is supplied by Lemma 3.0.6, with the cited obstruction-theoretic input.
An isolated q-subscript inconsistency on page 24 is read in the displayed tower; no independent mathematical failure is inferred from that typographical issue.

proof_coverage.claim: First-stage transitivity for an arbitrary stable bundle
reasoning: Fix the stable bundle xi and its determinant L. After changing the basepoint, the action obstruction is Delta(M)=c_d(M)+sum_{r=1}^{d-1} c_r(M)c_{d-r}(xi).
For the selected Suslin class S_d, the lower Chern classes vanish and the degree-d class is (d-1)! times kappa_d. Thus all the terms involving lower Chern classes of M disappear.
The cohomological-dimension bound makes kappa_d onto the relevant H^{d-1}(X,K_d^M). Lemma 4.0.3 gives divisibility by (d-1)! under the main characteristic hypothesis, so Delta is onto.
The orbit set at this first stage is consequently a single point for every xi, including nontrivial determinant and nonzero lower Chern classes.
For d=3, one only needs this surjectivity of kappa_d as a pointed-set map. The proof does not need to import the d>=4 group structure of [X,A^d minus 0] into this step.
external_inputs: The formula for the Chern classes of Suslin classes and the cited formula for the shifted action are not independently reconstructed from universal characteristic classes.

proof_coverage.claim: Second-stage transitivity and the actual lifting of the selected loops
proof_coverage.status: Checked; no unjustified lifting of arbitrary K_1 classes is assumed
reasoning: Corollary 3.0.4 identifies H^d(pi_d F_{d-1}(L)) with the stable target H^d(K_{d+1}^M). The relevant square compares the upper action from loops of E_{d-1} with the lower action from loops of BGL.
H^d(X,K_{d+1}^M) is a quotient of a direct sum of k^times at closed points, so it is divisible. For a requested class alpha, choose beta with d! beta=alpha; uniqueness of beta is unnecessary.
The class S_{d+1} constructed from beta has all Chern classes in degrees <=d equal to zero. The formula from the first stage therefore shows that its translated loop has zero first-stage obstruction.
Exactness supplies a lift of this particular loop to E_{d-1}. Its image under the upper boundary is alpha by the commutative square and the right-hand isomorphism.

This proves upper-boundary surjectivity without assuming every stable automorphism lifts. Together with the first-stage result and tower truncation, it proves the stated cancellation consequence, conditional on Section 4.

proof_coverage.claim: Abelian exact sequence and reduction of unimodular rows to a smooth threefold
proof_coverage.status: Checked in the explicitly stated range d>=4
reasoning: Equation (4.0.1) is promoted to an exact sequence of abelian groups only after establishing the stable cohomotopy range. The identification with Um_d(X)/E_d(X) is compatible with the group structure by the cited comparison theorem.
In Lemma 4.0.2, a Bertini move arranges that a_4,...,a_d cut out a smooth affine threefold Y. The triple of remaining coordinates gives a unimodular row on Y.

Appending the fixed tail induces a well-defined map Um_3(Y)/E_3(Y)->Um_d(X)/E_d(X). Changing lifts of the first three coordinates by multiples of the tail is effected by elementary operations, so it does not change the resulting class.

The cited divisibility of the threefold group and the homomorphism property of this map show divisibility of the original class. Algebraic closedness supplies sqrt(-1), as required for the group-law compatibility.
The argument is used only for d>=4; the three-dimensional final case is handled separately.
external_inputs: The Bertini moving theorem, the threefold divisibility theorem, and the comparison of group structures are retained as stated deep inputs.

proof_coverage.status: Spectral-sequence positions and the final diagram chase checked
reasoning: For a prime ell different from char(k), use the kernel/image factorization of multiplication by ell on K_d^M. The two short exact sequences produce the horizontal and vertical maps of (4.0.4).

The coniveau spectral sequence has E_2^{a,b}=H_Zar^a(X,H_et^b) in the region 0<=a<=b<=d. At (d-1,d) and (d-2,d), there are no incoming differentials because their potential sources have b>d, and no outgoing differentials because the targets have a>b or a>d.
Their total degrees are 2d-1 and 2d-2, both greater than d for d>2, so they vanish by affine etale cohomological dimension.

For the term (d-1,d-1), the only possible incoming differential is d_2 from (d-3,d); all higher incoming sources have second coordinate greater than d. Outgoing differentials leave the allowed region. Vanishing of the abutment therefore makes this d_2 onto.

Norm residue identifies K_d^M/ell with the appropriate etale-cohomology sheaf. The cited Suslin torsion statement and the BVPW compatibility identify the dotted connecting map with that surjective d_2.
The two outer K_d^M/ell cohomology terms vanish. The remaining obstruction H^d(X, _ell K_d^M) vanishes because its last Rost-Schmid term is _ell K_0^M(k)=0.
The displayed diagram then gives both injectivity and surjectivity of multiplication by ell on H^{d-1}(K_d^M). The uniqueness is essential for the later kernel argument.
external_inputs: Norm residue, Suslin's torsion identification, and the BVPW comparison of the connecting morphism with d_2 are cited results not independently re-proved.

proof_coverage.claim: Divisibility of the cohomotopy kernel, H^{d-2}(K_d^M), and the target top cohomology
proof_coverage.status: Diagram chases and extension argument checked
reasoning: For 0->H->G->M->0 with G ell-divisible and M ell-torsion-free, an ell-root g of h in G has image in M killed by ell, hence its image is zero. Thus H is ell-divisible. The paper supplies the stronger unique ell-divisibility of M, so the argument applies.

In Lemma 4.0.5, first choose a lift b of the requested lower-right class. Its horizontal obstruction lies in H^{d-1}(_ell K_d^M). Subtract the image of a class from H^{d-3}(K_d^M/ell) whose dotted image equals that obstruction.
This correction does not change the requested lower-right class, by vertical exactness, and it kills the horizontal obstruction. A horizontal lift then gives the desired ell-root.

The group H^d(pi_d(A^d minus 0)) is an extension of the resulting divisible kernel by a quotient of H^{d-2}(K_d^M). Quotients and extensions of ell-divisible abelian groups are ell-divisible, proving Proposition 4.0.6.

proof_coverage.status: A wrong Milnor-K index is confirmed; a complete local repair is supplied in FND01
reasoning: The first nonzero homotopy sheaf of A^{d+2} minus 0 is pi_{d+1}=K_{d+2}^MW. Page 35 instead prints K_{d+1}^MW and then K_{d+1}^M.
After replacing these two weights by d+2, top cohomology of K_{d+2}^M is a quotient of a direct sum of K_2^M(k), hence divisible.
Lemma 2.4.1, with sphere dimension d+2 and homotopy degree d+1, makes the corresponding cokernel annihilated by (d+1)!. A divisible group with this bounded exponent is zero.
The two short exact sequences on page 35 then do yield the stabilization isomorphism. This correction does not refute the lemma's conclusion.

proof_coverage.status: The displayed three-term inference needs an extra justification; it is completed under the main theorem's d!-invertibility hypothesis in COMPLETION01
reasoning: The sheaf sequence B->D->E is exact, but H^d is not generally left exact on a three-term sequence that is not known to end in zero. The printed sentence saying it suffices to bound H^d(B) suppresses a cokernel term.
Let A=K_{d+1}^M on X and r:E=pi_d(GL_{d+1})->A. Under d! invertible, A and H^{d-1}(A) are d!-divisible by the independent Rost-Schmid argument recorded in COMPLETION01.
The Suslin map t:A->E satisfies r t=d! id. It follows that r and H^{d-1}(r) are onto.

For J=ker(r), the sequence 0->J->E->A->0 then makes H^d(J)->H^d(E) injective. The sequence 0->B->D->J->0 identifies the desired cohomology kernel with the image of H^d(B). Lemma 2.4.1 bounds that image by d!.

No counterexample to Lemma 4.0.8 or to cancellation is established. The added argument covers the characteristic range needed by the main theorem; the wider char(k)!=2 statement when char(k) divides d! is outside this completed repair.

proof_coverage.claim: Factorial annihilation of the target group
proof_coverage.status: Checked conditional on the cited Hermitian-K input and the kernel comparison
reasoning: The stabilized Suslin map factors through the relevant space representing Hermitian K-theory. Its degree-d homotopy sheaf is GW_{d+1}^d, and the cited vanishing of its H^d makes the stabilized image zero.
Stable connectivity identifies the stable H^d pi_d(GL) target with H^d pi_d(GL_{d+2}); Lemma 4.0.7 gives the previous one-step comparison.
Lemma 4.0.8 then makes the image in H^d pi_d(GL_d) d!-torsion. Applying the first-row map and the composite identity r_d u'_d=(d-1)! gives d!(d-1)! annihilation of the original class.
The use of the power-map formula at homotopy degree d is valid for d>=4. Combined with Proposition 4.0.6 and d! invertible, the group must vanish.
external_inputs: The Hermitian-K factorization and H^d(X,GW_{d+1}^d)=0 from the cited work are not independently re-proved. The report must state this dependency.
proof_coverage.boundary: The cancellation theorem needs char(k)>d or zero. Proposition 4.0.9 advertises the wider char(k)!=2 range; the supplied completion of its kernel substep was only verified in the main theorem range.

proof_coverage.status: Checked as a distinct boundary proof
reasoning: The argument uses the stated exact sequence T_5->pi_3(A^3 minus 0)->GW_4^3->0 and the cited pullback description of T_5.
That pullback gives 0->I^6->T_5->K_5^M/24->0. On a smooth threefold over the stated algebraically closed field, H^3(I^6)=0 by the earlier I-power vanishing.
The last Rost-Schmid term for K_5^M/24 in degree 3 is K_2^M(k)/24, which is zero because every symbol is 24 times a symbol after choosing a 24th root of one entry in algebraically closed k.
Consequently H^3(T_5)=0; together with the cited H^3(GW_4^3)=0, this proves the required H^3(pi_3(A^3 minus 0)) vanishing.
This argument avoids the stable cohomotopy range that would fail for m=d=3. The main theorem already excludes characteristic 3 by 3! invertible.
external_inputs: The AFW20 pullback description and the cited GW cohomology vanishing are accepted external inputs, not independently reconstructed in this review.

checked_derivations.title: Completing the cohomology-kernel inference in Lemma 4.0.8 under the main theorem's hypotheses
assumptions: X is smooth affine of dimension d>=4 over algebraically closed k.
N=d! is invertible in k. This is the main cancellation theorem's characteristic restriction.
Use the paper's cited norm-residue, Rost-Schmid, contraction, and Suslin-map inputs. No author code is involved.
notation: The long exact homotopy sequence gives D->E --r--> A; the preceding cokernel B injects into D. The Milnor-Witt sheaf at this spot equals A on X by the I-power vanishing.
There is a Suslin-induced map t:A->E with r t=N id_A. This follows from the coordinate-power relation with sphere dimension d+1, homotopy degree d, and sqrt(-1) in k.

steps.statement: A is N-divisible as a sheaf on the small Nisnevich site of X.
steps.proof: For each prime ell dividing N, ell differs from char(k). Every generic field of a scheme etale over X has transcendence degree at most d over algebraically closed k, so its ell-cohomological dimension is at most d. Norm residue gives K_{d+1}^M(F)/ell=H_et^{d+1}(F,mu_ell^{tensor(d+1)})=0. The strictly A1-invariant quotient sheaf K_{d+1}^M/ell is unramified and therefore vanishes on these schemes when its generic values vanish. Thus A/ell=0, and multiplying the prime factors gives N-divisibility.

Each closed point x is k-rational and lies on an integral affine curve C in X. Normalize C; its normalization is a smooth affine curve, finite over C, with a k-point above x. For a smooth affine curve over an algebraically closed field, Pic is divisible: embed it in a smooth projective curve, use a boundary k-point to remove the degree part, and use divisibility of the k-points of the Jacobian. Pushforward of an N-root of the point class from the normalized curve gives an N-root of [x] in CH_0(X). Closed points generate CH_0, so the entire group is divisible.

steps.statement: H^d(X, _ell A)=0 for every prime ell dividing N.
steps.proof: Contraction of the ell-torsion sheaf is exact in the strictly A1-invariant category. The final Rost-Schmid term for _ell A is the sum of _ell K_1^M(k)=mu_ell(k) over the closed points. Choose a primitive root tau to identify each summand with Z/ell. In codimension d-1, the torsion symbols {tau,f} in _ell K_2^M(k(C)) have residues tau^{ord_z(f)} (up to the consistent boundary convention). Their boundaries include the principal-divisor relations modulo ell. Consequently the top cohomology is a quotient of CH_0(X)/ell, which is zero by Step 2.

Step 1 makes 0->_ell A->A --ell-->A->0 a short exact sequence on X. Its long exact cohomology sequence and Step 3 make multiplication by ell onto on H^{d-1}(X,A). Apply this successively to the prime factors of N.

steps.statement: Both r:E->A and H^{d-1}(r) are onto.
steps.proof: For a local section a of A, choose an N-root b by Step 1, and r(t(b))=a. For a cohomology class alpha in H^{d-1}(A), choose an N-root beta by Step 4 and use H^{d-1}(t)(beta). The composite on cohomology is multiplication by N.

steps.statement: The desired cohomology kernel is the image of H^d(B).
steps.proof: Set J=ker(r)=im(D->E). From 0->J->E->A->0, the surjectivity of H^{d-1}(r) implies that H^d(J)->H^d(E) is injective. From 0->B->D->J->0, cohomological dimension at most d gives exact H^d(B)->H^d(D)->H^d(J)->0. Combining these sequences proves ker[H^d(D)->H^d(E)]=im[H^d(B)->H^d(D)].

steps.statement: That kernel is annihilated by N=d!.
steps.proof: The preceding homotopy segment gives pi_{d+1}(GL_{d+1})->pi_{d+1}(A^{d+1} minus 0)->B->0. Top cohomology is right exact here. Lemma 2.4.1, with sphere dimension d+1 and homotopy degree d+1, makes its cohomology cokernel N-torsion. This cokernel is H^d(B), so Step 6 gives the required bound.

checked_derivations.range_check: For the last Suslin bound, 2<=d+1<=2(d+1)-4 holds when d>=3. For r t=N id at degree d, the range holds when d>=2. The actual use here is d>=4.
checked_derivations.limitation: This is a proof completion under N invertible. It is not a claimed proof of the broader char(k)!=2 lemma when char(k) divides N; that case would require additional characteristic-p input or another argument.

checked_derivations.title: Symbol divisibility used in the corrected stabilization step and in dimension three
checked_derivations.proof: For algebraically closed k, any a in k^times and positive N admit c in k^times with c^N=a, including N divisible by the characteristic. Multilinearity gives {a,b}=N{c,b} in Milnor K_2(k). As symbols generate K_2, this proves divisibility by N. It does not assert that multiplication by N is injective. It proves K_2(k)/N=0, which is all the two uses require.

limitations: This is a scientific initial review of the exact arXiv v2 PDF, not an audit of all previous literature and not a claim about a possibly different journal version.
All 39 page texts were read, and 24 decisive page images were actually inspected. The other 15 rendered page images are not claimed as visually inspected.

The proof depends on deep cited inputs: motivic representability and homotopy sheaf calculations; the Suslin matrix construction and its Chern classes; the Bertini and threefold divisibility theorems; norm residue and the Suslin/BVPW cohomological compatibility; Hermitian K-theory factorization and Grothendieck-Witt cohomology vanishing.
